binary.note: bin_0-2 int 0/1; bin_3 T/F, bin_4 Y/N — map to 0/1

nominal_low_card.note: human-readable labels (colors, shapes, animals, countries, instruments); no intrinsic order

nominal_high_card.note: opaque 9-char hex hashes; carry no external semantics

known_orders.ord_2: Freezing < Cold < Warm < Hot < Boiling Hot < Lava Hot
known_orders.ord_5: 2-character strings — order by (char1, char2) ASCII; also decomposable into two separate ordinal sub-features

cyclical.note: day 1-7, month 1-12; integer-coded cycles with no year column — no absolute timeline

test_window.evidence: no date/timestamp column; day/month are anonymized cyclical integers with no year anchor. id is a contiguous row counter (train 0-299999, test 300000-499999) with no semantic content. Category level sets are near-identical between train and test (all low-card columns identical; nom_8 4 unseen levels, nom_9 87 unseen out of ~12k) — consistent with a random split of one synthetic population, not a temporal or group split.

split_policy.forbidden: any target/likelihood encoding fit on the full training set before splitting — encoders must be fit inside each training fold only (out-of-fold target encoding). This is the dominant leakage risk for this task, not the split scheme itself.
split_policy.rationale: iid split, no time or group structure to preserve; 30.6% positive rate makes stratification cheap insurance rather than a necessity

metric.name: AUC-ROC
traps: rank-based: absolute calibration is irrelevant, and no decision threshold should be tuned
invariant to any monotone transform of scores — blend on the rank scale (or logit scale) rather than raw probabilities when members are differently calibrated
class balance 30.6% is not imbalanced enough to justify resampling; resampling would only distort probabilities without helping the ranking
submission must contain probabilities/scores, not hard 0/1 labels

external_data.rationale: competition rules permit external data (config.yaml special_rules.external_data_allowed: true), but no whitelist source can be joined usefully. The high-cardinality nominals are opaque hashes; the only real-world-named column, nom_3 (Finland/Russia/Canada/...), has no year, date, or currency column to join a World Bank / holiday / exchange-rate table against, and day/month carry no year anchor. ISO country tables would add only a static regrouping of a 6-level column already fully observed in both splits. The data is a synthetic all-categorical benchmark: signal lives entirely in the encoding of the provided columns.

data_level: explicit ordinal integer mappings for ord_0-ord_5 using the known orders above (do NOT let label-encoding assign arbitrary alphabetical codes to ord_1/ord_2)
split ord_5 into its two constituent characters as separate ordinal features, plus keep the joined 192-level category
cyclical sin/cos encoding of day and month, kept alongside the raw categorical version
out-of-fold (CV-safe) target encoding with smoothing for nom_5-nom_9; unseen test levels (4 in nom_8, 87 in nom_9) must fall back to the global prior — verify the fallback path explicitly
frequency / count encoding for the high-cardinality nominals as a leakage-free complement to target encoding
sparse one-hot expansion of every column (~16k columns) as the feature space for a regularized linear member
pairwise crosses among the low-cardinality columns (bin_*, nom_0-4, ord_0-2, day, month) as new categorical levels, then target/count encode them
model_level: regularized logistic regression on the full sparse one-hot matrix as a first-class member, not just a baseline — an all-categorical target with no continuous interactions is the archetype where a linear model on one-hot competes with or beats GBDT

GBDT with native categorical handling (LightGBM categorical_feature / CatBoost ordered target statistics) as the strong tree baseline — per TASK-CAT-ONLY, native handling is where the measurable gain sat on s3e11
CatBoost is the natural fit here (ordered boosting is exactly a leakage-safe target encoder) — include for encoding diversity, not merely for model diversity
TASK-BLEND-DECOR: add one shallow, heavily regularized, different-library member (e.g. the linear one-hot model) as a decorrelator before optimizing blend weights
blend by rank-averaging or logit-averaging OOF predictions since the metric is rank-based
no threshold tuning, no probability calibration step — both are no-ops under AUC

rejected_task_priors.reason: no date column and no train/test time ordering — test is an iid split
day/month are anonymized cyclical categoricals, not a daily series; no store/product/country-date keys
positive rate 30.6%, far above the ~2% trigger
metric is AUC, not an MAE-family metric
23 categorical columns, 300k rows — rows greatly exceed columns

eda_must_resolve: confirm the iid hypothesis: compare per-column level distributions train vs test (a chi-square / adversarial-validation AUC near 0.5 confirms it)
measure univariate target rates per level for ord_1/ord_2/ord_3/ord_4 to confirm the assumed orderings are monotone in the target; if not monotone, treat them as nominal
quantify how much of nom_9's 11,981 levels are singletons — this sets the smoothing prior for target encoding
check whether day/month show a monotone or cyclical target-rate pattern to decide whether the sin/cos encoding earns its place
not_recorded: official competition rules page text — external-data permission taken from config.yaml special_rules, not re-verified against the live rules page (no discussions/kernels read per Stage 0.5 constraints)
real-world calendar semantics of day/month — no year column, so whether day=1 means Monday or Sunday and whether month indexes a real calendar is undeterminable from the provided files
generative process / true feature-target relationship of the synthetic data — undeterminable without modeling
